authority_boundary.downstream_responsibility: pricing, risk, scenario, policy-sensitivity, market-model sensitivity and quantitative consequences

market_model_boundary.principle: physical quantity and market price are separate analytical processes
market_model_boundary.physical_quantity: SPK consumes an explicitly admitted Policy Lab quantity and never derives market price from that quantity implicitly
market_model_boundary.forward_curve_extrapolation: rejected by default; only interpolation inside observed maturities is supported
market_model_boundary.forward_pricing_provenance: forward-option values retain curve source, source hash, observation time, price unit, and interpolation rule
market_model_boundary.unit_conversion: implicit conversion is rejected; explicit conversion objects are required and carry deterministic identities
market_model_boundary.negative_price_support: AEMO empirical inputs, forward curves, Bachelier, Ornstein-Uhlenbeck, and spike-scenario surfaces permit negative market prices; Black-76 explicitly rejects non-positive forwards

artifact_protocol.scenario_binding: market-risk artifacts bind the deterministic scenario_set_id used for valuation

policy_sensitivity.principle: governance policy is an explicit analytical dimension, never a hidden default
policy_sensitivity.blocked_outcomes: retained for comparison but never priced
policy_sensitivity.multi_policy_pricing: all admitted policies can be valued under one common market/model assumption set

model_sensitivity.principle: market-model choice is an explicit analytical dimension distinct from evidence and policy
model_sensitivity.comparison: multiple named market-price scenario sets can be compared under one fixed admitted quantity and contract
model_sensitivity.risk_summary: mean, standard deviation, 5th/50th/95th percentiles, negative-value probability, and protection value relative to merchant exposure

joint_volume_price_risk.principle: realized physical quantity and market price can vary jointly without being collapsed into one stochastic variable
joint_volume_price_risk.authority_cap: Policy Lab-admitted quantity is an upper bound for policy-bound realized-quantity scenarios
joint_volume_price_risk.dependence: paired scenarios preserve empirical quantity-price dependence and report correlation when defined

reproducibility.scenario_sets: market-price and joint volume-price scenario values can be bound to deterministic manifests with source/model/seed declarations; CLI workflows can build, verify and consume those identities
reproducibility.analytic_monte_carlo: Black-76 and Bachelier analytic values can be checked against seeded Monte Carlo estimators under matching assumptions
reproducibility.historical_replay: MAE, RMSE, bias and correlation diagnostics are available for aligned observed/modeled series
reproducibility.interpretation: implementation consistency and replay diagnostics do not establish empirical model correctness

aemo_nem.source_authority: Australian Energy Market Operator public NEM DISPATCH.PRICE
aemo_nem.source_identity: SHA-256 of the exact local CSV or ZIP file bytes
aemo_nem.network_access: none; adapter consumes an explicitly supplied local file
aemo_nem.market_clock: AEST UTC+10 fixed; period-ending timestamps converted to UTC
aemo_nem.transformations: region selection, intervention filtering, timestamp conversion and ordering only; no clipping, aggregation, winsorization or unit conversion

supported_surface.principle: the canonical 0.5 quantitative spine is validated separately from retained historical/compatibility modules
supported_surface.legacy_status: historical utilities remain available but are not implied to have the same support or coverage contract as the canonical spine

non_claims: SPK Derivatives is not a policy authority.
SPK Derivatives does not upgrade Policy Lab evidence assurance.
Policy sensitivity is not the same thing as market/model sensitivity or evidence truth.
Historical calibration does not automatically establish a risk-neutral pricing measure.
Analytic-versus-Monte-Carlo agreement validates implementation consistency under common assumptions, not market-model correctness.
A deterministic scenario identity establishes which scenarios were used, not their probability or authority.
Binding a scenario_set_id into a market-risk artifact proves input identity, not market truth or forecast quality.
An AEMO source hash proves which local file was consumed, not data completeness, finality, market-model correctness, or AEMO endorsement.
Mean-reverting jump/spike scenarios are scenario generators, not automatically a risk-neutral pricing measure.
Explicit unit conversion does not establish semantic equivalence between claims, certificates, credits, and physical energy.
Joint realized-quantity scenarios cannot expand Policy Lab-admitted authority.
Model output is not settlement, legal, regulatory, liquidity, or execution authority.
Ornstein-Uhlenbeck scenarios are not automatically a risk-neutral pricing measure.
Deterministic contract settlement arithmetic is not legal settlement authority or trade execution.
Repository-wide coverage includes retained historical modules and should not be confused with canonical-spine validation coverage.
The repository remains research/beta software rather than a production trading system.
